chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man in ihram who had intercourse with his wife in what is below the private part. He said: Upon him is a camel (as ransom), and he is not required to perform Hajj next year.

key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A camel (a specific type of animal sacrifice/ransom in Islamic law)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a man in ihram who has intercourse with his wife below the private part?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar clarifies the distinction between full penetration (jam') and partial intercourse (jima' duna al-farj) in determining the penalty for breaking ihram, prescribing a camel (badanah) rather than the heavier expiation for full union. Notably, it exempts the pilgrim from repeating Hajj the following year, a ruling that highlights the Shia juristic view that the obligation of Hajj is not nullified by this specific type of sexual act, contrasting with some Sunni schools. The narration, transmitted via Safwan ibn Yahya, underscores the precision of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in delineating degrees of ritual impurity and their corresponding legal consequences.
